title: feat(plugin-email): a host can decide where every SMTP transport the email plugin builds may connect
body:
Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`EmailServicePlugin` 新增构造选项 `smtpConnect`,宿主可借它决定插件构建的每一个 SMTP 传输能连到哪里——启动时构建的、由已保存的邮件设置构建的、以及「发送测试邮件」临时构建的,三处一律生效。
- 为什么改:宿主需要能决定插件构建的每一个 SMTP 传输的去向,包括由已保存设置构建的;按维护者裁决,在框架里开一个正式的宿主接缝,默认行为不变,策略归宿主。
- 风险与回滚:不传该选项时三处交给 nodemailer 的选项与今天逐字节相同(有字面量对照测试钉住);传了之后,`transportOptions` 中会自行选择连接或传输种类的键在构建时被拒并点名;策略放行时若没有交回套接字,该连接直接失败。回滚即还原本 PR,无数据或元数据迁移。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/transports/smtp.ts`(`buildSmtpOptions` 末尾的应用顺序、拒绝清单与 `admitOnlyWithSocket`)、`src/email-plugin.ts`(`buildTransport` / `buildSmtpTransport` 两个帮助方法及三处调用点)、`src/smtp-transport-construction.census.test.ts`(防止第四处构建绕过接缝)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-email exec vitest run src/transports/smtp.wire.test.ts`,预期全部通过,其中 8 条「a host connect policy」用例在真实 SMTP 会话上分别证明拒绝、无套接字的放行失败、放行、连接池与覆盖顺序。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

A host can decide where every SMTP transport the email plugin builds may connect, including transports built from saved mail settings.

- `EmailServicePlugin` takes a new constructor option, `smtpConnect` (`SmtpConnectPolicy`). It is applied to all three SMTP construction sites: the boot-built transport (`providerOptions` / `OS_EMAIL_SMTP_*`, through `makeTransport`), the live transport built from saved `mail` settings, and the one-shot transport the `mail/test` settings action builds.
- `SmtpConnectPolicy.getSocket` is nodemailer's own `getSocket` transport option. It is asked for every connection with the configured `host` and `port`, admits by handing back the socket it opened (`{ connection }`), and refuses with an error whose message is what the failed send and the `mail/test` answer report. An answer without a socket fails the connection with a fixed message (`SMTP_CONNECT_POLICY_NO_SOCKET`), and `SmtpConnectCallback` admits no `false`. The `mail/test` echo itself is unchanged.
- `SmtpTransportOptions` gains a first-class `connect` field and `MakeTransportOptions` an `smtpConnect` field. `buildSmtpOptions` applies the policy after `...transportOptions`, and while a policy is set it refuses at construction, naming the key, `transportOptions` carrying `send`, `proxy`, `url`, `sendmail`, `streamTransport`, `jsonTransport`, `SES`, `connection`, `socket`, a `tls` block that names a `socket` (whatever its value), or an OAuth2 `auth`. Without a policy those keys behave as before.
- Construction is routed through one place per kind: `makeTransport` (handed the policy by the plugin's `buildTransport`) and the plugin's `buildSmtpTransport`. A census test fails when a `new SmtpTransport(` or a `makeTransport(` call appears anywhere else in the package.
- An absent option omits the key (conditional spread): every site hands nodemailer exactly today's options.
- `SmtpConnectPolicy`, `SmtpConnectRequest` and `SmtpConnectCallback` are exported from the package entry. The package README gains a short section on the option.

Verified against the installed nodemailer 10.2.1 and the declared floor 10.1.4 (tarball read): `smtp-transport` and `smtp-pool` both take `options.getSocket` in their constructors and call it before each connection, and a returned `connection` is merged into the connection options, after which implicit TLS / STARTTLS run with SNI against the configured host name. The floor is not raised.

## Tests

- `src/transports/smtp.test.ts`, new describe `SmtpTransport — a host connect policy` (nodemailer stubbed): the policy reaches `createTransport` and is asked with the configured host and port; a `transportOptions.getSocket` cannot replace it; a refusal is the policy's own error; an answer of `false`, `undefined` or `{}` fails the connection; `secure` / `requireTLS` equal the no-policy values for implicit TLS, required STARTTLS and opportunistic STARTTLS; each of the nine keys plus an OAuth2 `auth` and a `tls` naming a `socket` is refused with the policy and passed through unchanged without it; a policy with no `getSocket` is refused; `makeTransport` carries the policy and omits it when absent; CONTROL literal for the no-policy options.
- `src/transports/smtp.wire.test.ts`, new describe over a real SMTP conversation (real nodemailer; the fake SMTP testkit now counts accepted connections): a refusing policy fails the send in its own words and the server accepts no connection; an answer of `false`, `undefined` or `{}` fails the send and the server accepts no connection; an admitting policy delivers over the socket it opened; two sends on a non-pooled transport ask the policy twice with host and port; `transportOptions: { pool: true }` still asks the policy; a `transportOptions.getSocket` is never asked.
- `src/email-plugin.mail-settings.test.ts`, new describe `a host SMTP connect policy reaches every SMTP transport the plugin builds`: boot-built; live after a settings save and after a second save; after the provider moves to `log` and back, and to `resend` and back; `mail/test` with an unsaved host and port different from the live one; a refusal surfaces in the `mail/test` answer; a settings snapshot carrying `getSocket` / `transportOptions` / `connect` keys cannot get past the policy (admitting fixtures open and hand back a real socket); CONTROL literal pins for all three sites without the option.
- `src/smtp-transport-construction.census.test.ts`: every construction goes through the seam, with a positive control.

## Acceptance notes

- No page under `content/docs/` documents `EmailServicePlugin` constructor options (`kernel/runtime-services/email-service.mdx` documents the `services.email` API only), so the option is documented in the package README, which ships in the tarball and which that page's readers are pointed to. `content/docs/references/` is untouched.
- Reading `packages/core/src/capability-providers.ts` (`providesCapability`, the `email` entry's identities `com.objectstack.service.email` / `EmailServicePlugin`) and `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (the capability loop's `if (hasPluginMatching(spec.identities)) continue;`): when the host registers its own `EmailServicePlugin`, the capability loop does not build a second one, so a constructor option on the host's instance is the one in force.
- The `mail/test` answer text is unchanged; a refusal reaches it through the transport's error message as before.
